stemMarkdown: A shopkeeper marks up the price of an article by 30% over its cost price. If the cost price is $180, what should be the marked price?
solutionMarkdown:
The markup is calculated as a percentage of the cost price. The marked price can be found by adding 30% of the $180 to itself.

Cost Price (CP) = \$180
Markup Percentage = 30%
Marked Price (MP) = CP + (30% of CP)
$$ MP = 180 + (0.3 \times 180) $$
